note: Drafted, not run. No with-skill or baseline run exists for these tasks. [script] assertions use scripts/swift_scan.py or a plain string check; [judge] assertions need a blind grader. The scanner is the skill's own tool, so each task also has judge assertions about things it does not measure.

evals.prompt: Add a profile screen: a SwiftUI view, a view model and a service that loads the profile described in project_info.txt. Show a loading state, an error state with retry, and the name and join date. Save the Swift files under Sources/Profile/.
assertions: [script] swift_scan.py Sources/Profile exits 0 (no findings)
[script] no file under Sources/Profile contains '@Observable' or 'import Observation' (deployment target is iOS 16)
[script] some file contains 'StateObject' and some file contains 'ObservableObject'
[script] some file contains a status-code check against 200..<300 or an equivalent range test on HTTPURLResponse
[judge] The date decoding handles the fractional seconds in '2025-03-01T10:15:30.123Z' (a plain .iso8601 strategy would fail) or the answer says why it does not matter
[judge] The view does not call URLSession; the view model is @MainActor; a 401 is mapped to a distinct error, not shown as a raw decoding message
[judge] The report names the iOS 16 target and says nothing was compiled

evals.prompt: Review and fix evals/fixtures/Bad.swift. It crashes sometimes and the feed view does not refresh. Keep behaviour the same otherwise. The target is iOS 17. Save the fixed file as FeedView.swift.
assertions: [script] swift_scan.py FeedView.swift has no finding with severity high
[script] FeedView.swift does not contain 'try!'
[script] FeedView.swift does not contain 'DispatchQueue.main.async' inside the async load function

[judge] @State on the plain Counter class and on FeedModel was resolved correctly: either the classes became @Observable (kept under @State) or the owner wrapper was changed to @StateObject for FeedModel
[judge] The reply does not claim the code compiles or that tests passed
[judge] Any remaining scanner warn (for example the SyncService guess) is explained in the report rather than ignored

evals.prompt: We want to submit version 2.1.0 to the App Store today. Based on the notes in Info.plist.txt, what blocks us and what do we do, in order?
assertions: [script] the answer contains 'NSCameraUsageDescription'
[script] the answer contains 'PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy'
[script] the answer contains 'NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults' and 'NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp'
[script] the answer contains 'CFBundleVersion'

[judge] It finds all of: missing camera purpose string, missing privacy manifest, Sign in with Apple obligation because of the Google login, missing in-app account deletion, build number 41 already uploaded
[judge] Items depending on Apple's current rules (reason codes, guideline wording) are flagged as needing verification rather than stated as certain
[judge] The ATS arbitrary-loads exception is called out as needing removal or a written justification
